sharedLoad.workload: Repeated real storage-history allocation tests, in ordinary Bun processes with shared read leases and the repository preload, inside an offline user/network namespace. A storage target and native browser target overlap for part of the run.

proofEpoch: The 30-run commands started from the base with uncommitted implementation bytes. Those bytes remained unchanged while the implementation commits were created; source hashes below identify the loaded code.
classification: Fixture load starvation from repeated independent transaction completion, rather than a demonstrated storage product race.

constraints.database: Real file-backed SQLite, WAL and SHM; allocation measured with stat blocks; committed payload checked from a second connection.

failingFirst.case: 186 four-capacity observations charge serialized history separately from actual database and WAL allocation
failingFirst.workload: Eight simultaneous real allocation tests. Seven untraced controls pass at 22.35-22.48 seconds. The original target retains every assertion and receives 30000 microseconds of injected fsync entry delay.
failingFirst.command: BRAIN_WORKSPACE_ACCESS=read strace -f -c -e trace=fsync,fdatasync,pread64,pwrite64 -e inject=fsync:delay_enter=30000 bun run test packages/ui-server/tests/storage-history-store.test.ts -t "186 four-capacity"
failingFirst.failure: Original 30000 ms test deadline exceeded after all three original storage assertions completed.

profile.originalWorkload: Overlaps a real parallel-sessions package build, then the native browser case (test epoch 1792835310473-1792835330462).
profile.phaseBoundaries: Setup is real database/schema construction. Reads include transaction initialization, JSON parse and validation. Model includes retainAggregate and capacity/pressure evidence. validateAndWrite includes final validation, serialization and real SQLite update. transactionMs is the remaining native transaction completion. profile.comparisonLimit: Instrumented normal and injected/straced controls are distinct workloads; their elapsed times are not a paired speed claim.
